title: NEET Class 11 Physics - Gravitation: Concept Practice and Assessment
concepts: Variation of g with Altitude and Depth

questions.question: Which statement best describes gravitation?
options: A repulsive force between charged bodies
A universal attractive force between masses
A force acting only on planets
A force acting only on falling objects
questions.explanation: Gravitation is the universal attractive interaction between any two bodies having mass.

questions.question: The gravitational force between two bodies acts along the
options: line joining their centres of mass
questions.explanation: For two bodies treated as particles or spherically symmetric bodies, gravitational force acts along the line joining their centres.

questions.question: Why does a person feel Earth's gravitational pull but usually not notice the gravitational pull between two books?
options: Gravity does not act on books
The gravitational force between ordinary small masses is extremely small
questions.explanation: Every mass attracts every other mass, but the force between ordinary objects is usually too small to notice.

questions.question: Which phenomenon is primarily explained by gravitation?
options: Motion of the Moon around Earth
questions.explanation: The Moon remains in orbit around Earth because of Earth's gravitational attraction.

questions.question: Near Earth, the term 'gravity' usually refers to
options: the gravitational attraction experienced by objects near Earth
questions.explanation: Gravity is the gravitational attraction experienced near a celestial body such as Earth.

questions.question: Two isolated spherical bodies attract each other gravitationally. If both bodies are present, the forces they exert on each other are
options: equal in magnitude and opposite in direction
equal in magnitude and same in direction
questions.explanation: By Newton's third law, the gravitational forces on the two bodies are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction.

questions.question: Which statement is correct about gravitational interaction?
options: It can act across empty space
It acts only when bodies are moving
questions.explanation: Gravitational interaction is a long-range force and can act through empty space.

questions.question: A satellite orbiting Earth is continuously accelerating because
options: Earth's gravity continuously changes the direction of its velocity
there is no force on it
questions.explanation: Even in a circular orbit with constant speed, the velocity direction changes, producing centripetal acceleration supplied by gravity.

questions.question: Which pair contains two phenomena that both arise from gravitation?
questions.explanation: Tides and planetary orbits are both consequences of gravitational interactions.

questions.question: If all masses in the universe suddenly lost their mass, gravitational interactions would
questions.explanation: Gravitational attraction depends on mass, so with zero mass there would be no gravitational interaction.

questions.question: Kepler's first law states that a planet moves around the Sun in
options: a circular path with the Sun at the centre
an elliptical orbit with the Sun at one focus
a parabolic path with the Sun at the centre
questions.explanation: The orbit of a planet is an ellipse with the Sun at one of its foci.

questions.question: According to Kepler's second law, the line joining a planet to the Sun sweeps
questions.explanation: Kepler's second law states that the radius vector sweeps out equal areas in equal intervals of time.

questions.question: Kepler's third law gives the relation between a planet's period T and semi-major axis a as
questions.explanation: For planets orbiting the same Sun, T²/a³ is constant.

questions.question: A planet moves fastest when it is
options: at the centre of the Sun
at the midpoint of its orbit
questions.explanation: Equal areas are swept in equal times, so the planet must move faster when it is closer to the Sun.

questions.question: If the orbital radius of a planet is increased by a factor of 4, its orbital period becomes
questions.explanation: Using T² ∝ r³, T' / T = 4^(3/2) = 8.

questions.question: A planet sweeps an area of 10^10 m² in 5 days. How much area will it sweep in the next 10 days if no external torque acts?
questions.explanation: Equal areas are swept in equal times, so twice the time gives twice the area: 2×10^10 m².

questions.question: For two planets orbiting the same star, T1 = 2T2. The ratio of their semi-major axes a1/a2 is
At perihelion, compared with aphelion, a planet has
options: smaller speed and smaller angular speed
greater speed and greater angular speed about the Sun
the same speed but different direction
questions.explanation: The planet is closest at perihelion and moves fastest; its angular rate about the Sun is also greater.

questions.question: If the semi-major axis of a planet's orbit becomes 9 times larger around the same star, its period becomes
Kepler's laws are most directly applicable to the idealized motion of planets when
options: the central star's gravity dominates the motion
questions.explanation: Kepler's laws describe orbital motion when the central body's gravitational influence dominates.

questions.question: The magnitude of gravitational force between masses m1 and m2 separated by distance r is
questions.explanation: Newton's law of gravitation is F = Gm1m2/r².

questions.question: If the distance between two masses is doubled, their gravitational force becomes
questions.explanation: Since F ∝ 1/r², doubling r makes the force one-fourth.

questions.question: If one of two masses is tripled while distance remains unchanged, gravitational force becomes
questions.explanation: Force is directly proportional to each mass.

questions.question: If both masses are doubled and the separation is unchanged, force becomes
questions.explanation: F ∝ m1m2, so doubling both gives a factor of 4.

questions.question: For two point masses, if the separation is reduced to half, the force becomes
questions.explanation: F ∝ 1/r², so replacing r by r/2 multiplies force by 4.

questions.question: Two masses 2 kg and 3 kg are 1 m apart. Taking G = 6.67×10^-11 N m² kg^-2, the force is approximately
questions.explanation: F = G(2)(3)/1² = 6G = 4.002×10^-10 N. Thus the correct value is 4.00×10^-10 N.

questions.question: Two bodies attract with force F. If their separation is increased by 3 times, the new force is
If the product m1m2 is kept constant while their separation is doubled, the gravitational force
questions.explanation: With m1m2 constant, F ∝ 1/r²; doubling r reduces F to F/4.

questions.question: Two equal masses each exert a gravitational force F on each other. If both masses become three times their original values, the new force is
questions.explanation: Both masses are multiplied by 3, so the product is multiplied by 9.

questions.question: For a spherically symmetric body, outside the body its gravitational attraction can be treated as if its mass were concentrated at
questions.explanation: For points outside a spherically symmetric body, the gravitational field is equivalent to that of a point mass at its centre.

questions.question: The SI unit of G is
questions.explanation: G has SI unit N m² kg^-2.

questions.question: The approximate value of G is
questions.explanation: The universal gravitational constant is approximately 6.67×10^-11 N m² kg^-2.

questions.question: Which statement correctly compares G and g?
options: G is universal, while g depends on location
g is universal, while G depends on location
Both depend only on object mass
questions.explanation: G is universal; acceleration due to gravity g varies with the celestial body and location.

questions.question: The dimensions of G are
questions.explanation: From F = Gm1m2/r², G = Fr²/m², giving [M^-1 L^3 T^-2].

questions.question: The numerical value of G is approximately the same
questions.explanation: G is a universal constant and does not depend on location.

questions.question: If the value of G were measured in a different unit system, its numerical value would
options: change, while the physical constant remains the same
questions.explanation: Numerical values depend on the chosen units, while the physical constant is unchanged.

questions.question: From F = Gm1m2/r², the SI dimensions of G are obtained by
questions.explanation: Rearranging gives G = Fr²/(m1m2).

questions.question: If G were larger while two masses and their separation remained unchanged, the gravitational force would
questions.explanation: Since F is directly proportional to G, a larger G produces a larger force.

questions.question: Which quantity has the SI unit m s^-2 rather than N m² kg^-2?
questions.explanation: Acceleration due to gravity g is measured in m s^-2; G has unit N m² kg^-2.

questions.question: The small numerical magnitude of G in SI mainly indicates that
options: gravitational interaction between ordinary small masses is weak
questions.explanation: The small value of G leads to very small gravitational forces for ordinary laboratory-scale masses.

questions.question: The acceleration of a freely falling body near Earth's surface, neglecting air resistance, is approximately
questions.explanation: Near Earth's surface, g is approximately 9.8 m/s².

questions.question: For a body of mass m near Earth's surface, the gravitational force is
questions.explanation: Weight or gravitational force near Earth's surface is W = mg.

questions.question: Ignoring air resistance, two bodies of different masses dropped from the same height have
questions.explanation: In the same gravitational field, all freely falling bodies have the same acceleration when air resistance is neglected.

questions.question: The relation between Earth's mass M, radius R and surface acceleration g is
questions.explanation: From Newton's law, g = GM/R² at Earth's surface.

questions.question: If Earth's mass remains constant but its radius increases, surface g
questions.explanation: Since g = GM/R², increasing R decreases g.

questions.question: A body is dropped from rest near Earth's surface. Its acceleration, ignoring air resistance, is
questions.explanation: The acceleration is downward toward Earth's centre and has magnitude about 9.8 m/s².

questions.question: If Earth's mass were doubled while its radius stayed the same, surface g would become
questions.explanation: g = GM/R², so doubling M doubles g.

questions.question: If both Earth's mass and radius were doubled, the new surface acceleration would be
A freely falling object near Earth has acceleration independent of its
options: mass, when air resistance is neglected
questions.explanation: For a given location, gravitational acceleration is independent of the object's mass in ideal free fall.

questions.question: At the surface of a planet of mass M and radius R, if M/R² is four times Earth's value, the planet's surface g is
questions.explanation: Because g = G(M/R²), four times M/R² gives four times the surface acceleration.

questions.question: Which quantity is a measure of the amount of matter in a body?
questions.explanation: Mass is the amount of matter and is measured in kilograms.

questions.question: The SI unit of weight is
questions.explanation: Weight is a force, so its SI unit is newton (N).

questions.question: The weight of a body of mass m at a location where acceleration due to gravity is g is
questions.explanation: Weight W = mg.

questions.question: A person's mass on the Moon compared with Earth is
questions.explanation: Mass is an intrinsic property and does not change merely because g changes.

questions.question: A person's weight on the Moon is approximately
questions.explanation: Moon's surface g is approximately one-sixth of Earth's, so W = mg is approximately one-sixth.

questions.question: A 50 kg person is on Earth where g = 9.8 m/s². The person's weight is

A 5 kg object is taken from Earth to a place where g becomes half its original value. Its mass and weight become
questions.explanation: Mass remains 5 kg, while W = mg becomes half when g becomes half.

questions.question: Two objects have masses 2 kg and 5 kg at the same place. The ratio of their weights W1:W2 is
questions.explanation: At the same location g is common, so W1:W2 = m1:m2 = 2:5.

questions.question: An object is weightless in an orbiting spacecraft mainly because
options: there is no gravity anywhere in space
the spacecraft and object are in continuous free fall together
questions.explanation: The object and spacecraft accelerate together under gravity, producing apparent weightlessness.

questions.concept: Variation of g with Altitude and Depth
questions.question: At a height h above Earth's surface, the exact expression for g is
questions.explanation: The distance from Earth's centre is R+h, so g_h = GM/(R+h)².

questions.explanation: Using (1+h/R)^-2 ≈ 1-2h/R for h << R gives g_h ≈ g(1-2h/R).

questions.concept: Variation of g with Altitude and Depth
questions.question: At the centre of a uniform Earth, the value of g is
questions.explanation: By symmetry, gravitational pulls from all directions cancel at the centre; for a uniform Earth, g = 0 there.

questions.question: For a uniform Earth, inside the Earth at depth d, g is
questions.explanation: For a uniform spherical Earth, g_d = g(1-d/R).

questions.question: At a height equal to Earth's radius (h = R), surface g becomes
questions.explanation: g_h = GM/(2R)² = g/4.

questions.concept: Variation of g with Altitude and Depth
questions.question: At depth d = R/2 inside a uniform Earth, the acceleration due to gravity is

questions.explanation: The distance from Earth's centre becomes 2R, so g_h/g = R²/(2R)² = 1/4.

questions.concept: Variation of g with Altitude and Depth
questions.question: For small altitude h and depth d, which comparison is correct for equal values h = d?
options: Both changes in g have equal magnitude
Decrease due to altitude is approximately twice the decrease due to depth
Decrease due to depth is approximately twice the decrease due to altitude
questions.explanation: For h << R, altitude gives g_h ≈ g(1-2h/R), while depth gives g_d = g(1-h/R).

questions.concept: Variation of g with Altitude and Depth
questions.question: A body is moved from Earth's surface to a depth R/2 inside a uniform Earth. Its weight becomes
questions.explanation: Since g at depth R/2 is g/2 and mass is unchanged, weight becomes half.

questions.concept: Variation of g with Altitude and Depth
questions.question: At what depth inside a uniform Earth will g become 25% of its surface value?
questions.explanation: Set g_d/g = 1-d/R = 1/4. Thus d/R = 3/4, so d = 3R/4.

questions.question: Which force keeps a book resting on a table from floating away from Earth?
questions.explanation: Earth's gravitational attraction acts on the book.

questions.question: Gravitational force between two masses is always
questions.explanation: For ordinary positive masses, gravitational interaction is attractive.

questions.question: If the distance between two bodies becomes extremely large, their mutual gravitational force approaches
questions.explanation: Since gravitational force varies as 1/r², it approaches zero as r becomes very large.

questions.question: Which statement distinguishes gravity from gravitation?
options: B. Gravity acts only between charged bodies
C. Gravitation is universal; gravity commonly describes the local effect near a celestial body
questions.explanation: Gravitation is the universal attraction between masses, while gravity commonly refers to gravitational attraction near a celestial body.

questions.question: Why can the gravitational force of a star control the motion of a planet despite the large separation?
options: A. It acts only through contact
C. It stops beyond Earth's atmosphere
D. It is a long-range force
questions.explanation: Gravity is a long-range interaction and acts across large distances.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a gravitational phenomenon?
questions.explanation: Electric current is caused by electromagnetic effects, not gravity.

questions.question: The gravitational force between two isolated masses is directed
options: A. Perpendicular to the line joining centres
B. Tangential to the orbit always
C. Along the line joining centres
questions.explanation: The force acts along the line joining their centres.

questions.question: If one body is removed from a two-body gravitational system, the mutual gravitational force between the original pair becomes
options: D. The original mutual force no longer exists
questions.explanation: With one body absent, there is no pair of masses between which the original force can act.

questions.question: A planet and its moon attract each other. Which statement is correct?
options: A. They exert equal and opposite forces on each other
B. The planet exerts force but the moon does not
C. The moon's force is always zero
D. Only the heavier body attracts
questions.explanation: Both bodies exert equal and opposite gravitational forces on each other.

questions.question: Gravitational interaction is called universal because
options: A. Only planets attract one another
C. Every mass can gravitationally interact with every other mass
D. Gravity acts only inside galaxies
questions.explanation: Every object having mass can gravitationally interact with every other object having mass.

questions.question: The point in a planet's elliptical orbit closest to the Sun is called
questions.explanation: The closest point is perihelion.

questions.question: The point farthest from the Sun in an elliptical orbit is called
questions.explanation: The farthest point is aphelion.

questions.question: Kepler's second law is a consequence of conservation of
questions.explanation: The constant areal velocity follows from conservation of angular momentum.

questions.question: If a planet's distance from the Sun decreases while angular momentum is conserved, its speed
questions.explanation: At smaller radius, conservation of angular momentum requires greater tangential speed.

questions.question: For planets around the same Sun, which quantity is constant according to Kepler's third law?
questions.explanation: T²/a³ is constant for planets orbiting the same central star.

questions.question: If a planet takes 8 years to complete an orbit, its semi-major axis relative to a planet taking 1 year is
A planet's areal velocity is constant. If it sweeps 6×10^10 m² in 3 days, it sweeps in 5 days
questions.explanation: Area swept is proportional to time, so 6×10^10 × 5/3 = 10^11 m².

questions.question: If T²/a³ = 4 for one planet around a star, another planet around the same star must also have
questions.explanation: The same ratio T²/a³.

questions.question: A planet has orbital period 27 years. Its semi-major axis in AU, taking Earth's period as 1 year and semi-major axis as 1 AU, is
At aphelion, the planet's speed is lower than at perihelion because
options: A. It is farther from the Sun and angular momentum is conserved
C. It is farther from the Sun and angular momentum conservation gives lower speed
questions.explanation: Conservation of angular momentum requires greater speed at smaller orbital radius.

questions.question: If both masses are reduced to half while distance is unchanged, force becomes
questions.explanation: The product of masses becomes one-fourth, so force becomes one-fourth.

questions.explanation: Mass product is unchanged and distance doubles, so force becomes F/4.

questions.explanation: New factor = 1.1×1.1 = 1.21, so force is 1.21F.

questions.question: G is called universal because its value
options: A. It is independent of location
C. It depends on Earth's radius
D. It depends on the test mass
questions.explanation: G has the same physical value throughout the universe.

questions.question: The unit N m² kg^-2 can also be written dimensionally as
questions.explanation: It is equivalent to m³ kg^-1 s^-2.

questions.question: The dimensions of gravitational force are
questions.explanation: Force has dimensions ML T^-2.

questions.question: Which equation can be used to determine G experimentally?
questions.explanation: From F = Gm1m2/r², G = Fr²/(m1m2).

options: C. It gives force dimensions after multiplication by m1m2/r²
questions.explanation: Substitution gives [M^-1L^3T^-2][M²]/L² = MLT^-2, the dimension of force.

questions.question: The approximate SI value of G is
A quantity has unit m³ kg^-1 s^-2. It can represent

questions.question: Which factor does NOT determine the value of G itself?
questions.explanation: G is universal and is not changed by the masses or separation used in an experiment.

questions.question: If the measured force is doubled while masses and separation remain unchanged, the inferred value of G would
questions.explanation: Since G = Fr²/(m1m2), doubling F doubles the inferred value.

questions.question: Why is G much smaller numerically than g?
options: A. They are different physical quantities and cannot be compared as identical numerical constants
questions.explanation: They are different physical quantities with different dimensions and units; their numerical values are not directly comparable as the same kind of quantity.

questions.question: The direction of g near Earth's surface is
questions.explanation: Acceleration due to gravity is directed toward Earth's centre.

questions.question: For a freely falling object, the only force considered in ideal free fall is
questions.explanation: Neglecting air resistance, gravitational force is the only force.

questions.question: If a body is thrown vertically upward, its acceleration while moving upward is

questions.explanation: In the same gravitational field, acceleration is independent of mass.

questions.question: Mass is a scalar quantity whereas weight is
questions.explanation: Weight is a force and therefore has both magnitude and direction.

questions.question: If g at a location is zero, the weight of a body there is
questions.explanation: W = mg, so if g=0, weight is zero.

questions.explanation: Mass does not depend on the local gravitational field.

questions.question: If g increases by 20% while mass remains constant, weight increases by
questions.explanation: Weight is directly proportional to g, so it increases by 20%.

questions.question: Two objects have equal weights at the same location. Their masses must be
questions.explanation: At the same location, g is common, so equal W means equal m.

questions.question: A 60 kg student has weight 588 N where g=9.8 m/s². This student's mass on Moon is
questions.explanation: Mass is invariant under change of location, so it remains 60 kg.

questions.question: If an object has mass 8 kg and is on a planet where g=5 m/s², its weight is

questions.explanation: W is proportional to g, so it becomes 2.5×20 = 50 N.

questions.question: A spring balance measures the weight of an object. If taken from Earth to a place with smaller g, its reading
questions.explanation: A spring balance measures force, so its reading decreases when g decreases.

questions.question: Which statement is correct about mass and weight?
options: A. Both are measured in kg
C. Mass is intrinsic; weight is gravitational force
D. Weight is independent of g
questions.explanation: Mass is intrinsic and measured in kg; weight is gravitational force and measured in N.
